messages:
alex: Heads-up — CI failing on paged+flash variant build in the bookworm image. Seen on nightly run 1749814567.

maya: repro logs?

alex: Paste below. Build error during link for fused_flash_paged.so
```
[100/210] Linking fused_flash_paged.so
/usr/bin/ld: fused_flash_paged.o: in function `flash::paged::dispatch()':
fused_flash_paged.o:(.text+0x1a7): undefined reference to `__cxa_allocate_exception'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Looks like libstdc++/C++ ABI thing or toolchain mismatch.

devon: Hmm. Which container/toolchain does CI use vs local dev? Our Dockerfile uses gcc-12 in build image but CI matrix has an older bookworm base with gcc-11 preinstalled (we forgot to update). Could be differing -fabi-version/default libstdc++.

maya: Also seeing a couple of warnings earlier preserved in the log
```
warning: relocation against ".rodata" can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
```
We do build with -fPIC normally though.

alex: Minimal reproducer I ran locally:
```
docker run --rm -it quay.io/redwood/build-bookworm:latest /bin/bash
git clone ...
bazel build //runtime/kernels:flash_paged_fused --config=release
```
Link error happens inside container but not on my mac or our gcc-12 dev VMs.

priya: Could be that some dependencies are coming in prebuilt under different ABI (precompiled .a from third-party). We ship some third-party kernels as static libs for build speed.

devon: Check ar -t third_party/flash/kernels.a and run nm on objects.

alex: I checked — static archive was built in another CI job with gcc-12 and pushed to GCS. CI bookworm uses gcc-11 at link time. Mixed-compiler static archive -> shared object link with different C++ ABI => undefined refs.

maya: That explains it. Short term: make CI ensure consistent compiler across matrix or build static archives in the same job. Long term: avoid shipping compiler-bound static artifacts.

priya: Added note: KV-cache microbench failing in same CI run for a different test — likely unrelated but popped up at same time. Failure: tail latency regressed on batched-routes test.

devon: Profiling info (local perf):
- Fused kernel mode shows +6% throughput for seq<=1024
- For seq in [2048,8192] we see -8% throughput vs paged variant on A100-40
- L2 cache miss rates up ~12% when fused selected for mixed batches

maya: That matches our telemetry on prod canaries last week — increased latencies on long-seq model when fused kernels were auto-selected. Looks like kernel selection heuristics are too aggressive for certain batch distributions.

alex: Proposed immediate fixes:
1) CI: pin gcc version in bookworm image to 12 or rebuild third-party archives inside the same CI job.
2) Runtime: add a safety net in kernel selector — if seq>2048 and batch variance high, prefer paged kernel or use fallback with smaller micro-batches.
3) Add unit that rebuilds static kernel artifacts with the declared build toolchain as part of release job.

priya: For (2) we can tweak heuristic to consider (seq * avg_batch_size) and L2 miss estimate from previous windows. Implement quick flag guard: --prefer-paged-threshold=2096.

devon: I'll open a PR to add CI pin + rebuild step. We'll also add a small test to the kernel packaging job that runs `nm` against produced .a and checks for __cxa symbols presence and gcc version stamp in .comment of object file.

maya: Love the nm check. Also we should add a warning in packaging pipeline logs when static archives are built with different compilers than the runtime image.

alex: CI change landed in draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/492 (WIP). Need reviewers from infra.

sre-bot: deploy-bot posted: nightly-build failed on bookworm-11 matrix (job 8421)

devon: Quick mitigation: turn off fused-paged as default in routing policy for the next release (canary still enabled for perf team). Will add runtime flag `--kernel-default=fallback`.

maya: Also investigating linking warnings about PIC. Might be our static archive built with -fno-PIC inadvertently. Adding check in build to fail on missing -fPIC.

priya: KV cache regression — I captured a flamegraph: higher self-time in memcpy in kv-merge path when fused kernel chosen. Looks like fused kernel causes different tok alignment leading to more copies.

alex: Action items (summarized):
- devon: CI pin + rebuild artifacts, add nm/gcc stamp checks (ETA today)
- maya: Heuristic guard change + runtime flag (ETA tomorrow)
- priya: KV-cache microbench + flamegraphs for both kernels, post to perf dash (ETA EOD)
- infra: update bookworm image or add gcc-12 package

devon: Note: to reproduce locally you might need to force mixed-compiler artifact. I pushed a test script: infra/ci/repro/mix-toolchain.sh
```
# usage: ./mix-toolchain.sh build-archive push-gcs
# it builds third_party archive with gcc-12 then runs link in gcc-11 container
```

maya: After temporary revert of fused default on canary we saw tail p99 drop back to expected. Rolling that change into next hotfix.

alex: Thx all. Please @mention if you need me to hold the release.

priya: tagging @eng-ml for awareness (kernel perf and kv cache interplay). :eyes: 

devon: PR ready for CI changes, requesting infra review now. :rocket: 

alex: closing the thread when PR merges. Thanks!
